lessons: The fence must add chupa/journal.py. Its run_seq (journal.py:71) counts every STATE_TRANSITION into TERMINAL_STATES, so a run-less drought park advances the run sequence. Section 15 says such a park is never a run terminal, and section 6.3 derives the sequence from prior terminals.

Before re-implementing, fix the plan's 19.P4.provider-cooldown-failover closure to fence chupa/journal.py and its sequencing test. The ticket's own Definition of rejected says to repair the contract rather than work around a path outside the fence.
Do not add a caller-local run_seq workaround in the fenced modules. Restart reconciliation reads the same journal.py fold, so a local fix would make recovery sequence numbers disagree with dispatch.

Once journal.py is fenced, add a regression test: a pre-dispatch provider_drought park leaves run_seq unchanged, a mid-run drought terminal advances it, and restart harvest identity agrees with both cases.
